sourceLabel: Brian White, Peano Existence Theorem (Stanford Math 63CM notes)
preciseLocator: Theorem 1, proof Case 1 (bounded F) and Case 2 (truncation to a ball)
evidence: Builds Euler polygons x_k with step 1/k, shows M-Lipschitz (Claim 1) and uniformly bounded (Claim 2), Arzela-Ascoli subsequence, uniform continuity of F gives F(y_k)->F(x) uniformly (Claim 3), passes to the limit in the integral equation; Case 2 reduces local continuous F to the bounded case.
sketchProblem: Source treats autonomous x'=F(x) forward in time only; the sketch's F(t,y) on a cylinder with h=min(a,b/M) and backward time is a routine adaptation (add t as a variable), not written out.

evidence: Proves uniqueness: S={t: y1=y2} is nonempty and 'closed (why?)'; shows openness at t0 by local Lipschitz bound u<=M|int u| and 'By Gronwall's inequality' u=0. The closedness step is left to the reader and Gronwall's inequality itself is only invoked, not proved, in this file.

Shows |f+g|^p<=2^{p-1}(|f|^p+|g|^p) so the norm is finite, then writes ||f+g||_p^p<=int(|f|+|g|)|f+g|^{p-1}, applies Hölder to each term and divides by ||f+g||_p^{p-1}. Endpoint cases p=1 and p=infinity are not written out.

preciseLocator: Section 'Proof' > 'Proof by a direct convexity argument'
evidence: Applies convexity (Jensen) pointwise to |f+g|^p with weight t, integrates, and chooses t=||g||_p/(||f||_p+||g||_p); this is the sketch's normalization lambda=a/(a+b) in unnormalized form.
sketchProblem: Wikipedia's version does not normalize F=f/a, G=g/b explicitly but is the same convexity argument.

evidence: Checked Wikipedia (Hölder and convexity proofs only), MIT OCW 18.125 lecture 10 (no Minkowski proof), and a web search for a simple-function/monotone-convergence proof; no free source found that proves Minkowski by reducing to simple functions then the finite weighted l^p inequality.

sourceLabel: TIFR Analysis I (Goswami) Lecture XXV, Riesz-Markov
preciseLocator: Theorem 6.9 proof: Steps II (outer measure, Lemma 6.12 partition of unity), III (Borel measurability), IV (regularity), V (L(f)=int f dmu); uniqueness Step I
evidence: Defines mu*(U)=sup{L f: 0<=f<=1_U, supp f in U}, extends by infimum over open sets, proves subadditivity via partitions of unity, Caratheodory measurability of Borel sets, regularity, and L f=int f dmu by level-slice approximation f=sum f_n squeezed between mu(K_n) sums; uniqueness via Lemma 6.11. Proved for locally compact Hausdorff, which includes compact Hausdorff.
sketchProblem: Sketch says 'finite additivity on disjoint opens' then extension; source gets additivity via Caratheodory rather than a separate finite-additivity step. r1 and r3 overlap heavily (both use sup over C(K) functions on open sets).

sourceLabel: Measures and all that: a tutorial (arXiv 1409.2662)
preciseLocator: Section 2.8.2: Lemmas 2.156-2.161, Theorem 2.162, Theorem 2.164 (Dini step inside its proof)
evidence: Treats L as positive normed functional on vector lattice C(X) continuous from above (Dini shown inside Thm 2.164), extends to monotone limits L+, builds sets G and outer measure by Caratheodory, shows sigma(F) in B and L(f)=int f dmu with uniqueness; remark after Cor 2.163 notes the general case gives a Baire measure.
sketchProblem: Theorem 2.164 is stated for compact metric spaces; the same proof gives a Baire measure on compact Hausdorff K as the sketch's caveat says, but regularity/Borel extension for non-metrizable K is only referenced, not proved.

sourceLabel: Joel Feldman (UBC), Measure Theory notes Part 5
evidence: Simple functions by linearity, monotone convergence for Tonelli, positive/negative parts for Fubini are all written out. But the indicator case for general product-measurable E is proved by a monotone-class argument (Prop 5.8), not by approximating from rectangles.

sourceLabel: Joel Feldman (UBC), Measure Theory notes Part 5
evidence: Product measure from rectangles by Caratheodory, sections measurable (Prop 5.4), monotone-class proof that x->nu(E_x) is measurable and both iterated integrals equal mu x nu (finite then sigma-finite), then simple/monotone limits give Tonelli and positive/negative parts give Fubini.
sketchProblem: Source uses the monotone class lemma directly rather than uniqueness of extension from a pi-system, and uniqueness of mu x nu is only asserted in Def 5.1(d); same overall method.

evidence: Read Feldman Part 5, Stanford Math 205A supplement 2 (product outer measure, uses open/G_delta only in a remark) and ProofWiki/Wikipedia; none proves Fubini-Tonelli for Lebesgue measure via dyadic boxes and G_delta null sets.

sourceLabel: Notes on Harmonic Analysis Part I: The Fourier Transform (arXiv 1709.03377)
preciseLocator: Theorem 1.13 (Inversion Theorem) and its proof; also Wikipedia 'Fourier inversion theorem' Proof
evidence: Integrates f-hat against the Gaussian Fourier transform with Fubini to get (f * Gauss-Weierstrass kernel), lets the parameter go to 0: right side tends to f a.e. (approximate identity), left side tends to the inverse integral by dominated convergence. Wikipedia gives the same argument for continuous f.
sketchProblem: Source gets the result a.e. (and Wikipedia at continuity points), with approximate-identity convergence taken as known.

sourceLabel: Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes (Univ. of Illinois, arXiv 0903.3845)
preciseLocator: Ch. 15 (Fejer kernel, Thm 15.7, formula 15.18, 15.21) and Ch. 16 Theorem 16.2(a)
evidence: Writes the Fejer mean of the Fourier integral as F_lambda * f, uses positivity/mass of the Fejer kernel (integral of sin^2(x/2)/x^2 by parts) and approximate-identity convergence in L1, then dominated convergence using f-hat in L1 to identify the limit with the full inverse integral.
sketchProblem: Source obtains convergence in L1 and then a.e. via a subsequence, not pointwise at continuity points; the mass computation uses the Dirichlet integral rather than contour integration.

sourceLabel: Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes (Univ. of Illinois, arXiv 0903.3845)
evidence: Proves Plancherel on L1 intersect L2 via Gaussian damping and Fubini, extends by density to a bounded isometry on L2, then shows inversion on the dense set and bijectivity (unitary).
sketchProblem: Dense class used is L1 intersect L2 (and smooth compact support for inversion), not the Schwartz class named in the sketch; the Gaussian-damping/Fubini isometry step matches. Inversion step relies on Thm 16.2.
